rankings.blurb: Four Cornerstones including the most valuable RB and TE in the league, a franchise QB in Drake Maye, and a receiver room anchored by Puka Nacua and Tetairoa McMillan — this roster is absolutely stacked top to bottom. Yes, they overpaid for Jahmyr Gibbs (lost that trade by nearly 2,400 in value), but when your consolation prize is STILL having Gibbs, Maye, Nacua, and McBride, who's really crying? The only real knock is just one first-round pick in the vault, meaning they're all-in on the present — which is exactly the right call when your present looks like THIS. Everyone else is just audditioning to be the villain in ekleiner's championship highlight reel.

Eleven Cornerstones and Foundational pieces, Ja'Marr Chase and JSN as a literal WR1-WR2 combo from hell, Jayden Daniels and Justin Herbert splitting QB duties like some kind of deranged fantasy buffet — Sven is absolutely loaded at the skill positions. The RB room with Achane and Omarion Hampton is quietly elite, and Colston Loveland at TE is a sneaky dynasty dart. But those recent trades are concerning — three straight losses in the trade log, including getting absolutely smoked by Hernandez, suggests Sven might be the guy who builds a mansion and then leaves the front door unlocked. Fix the trading, Sven, and this is a championship roster.

Seven first-round picks and a raw value rank of number one on Dynastyze — Sinykin is playing 4D chess while everyone else is playing checkers, stockpiling Caleb Williams, Jaxson Dart, Jeremiyah Love, and Emeka Egbuka like he's collecting Infinity Stones. The Reload tag is accurate: there's massive upside here but it hinges on a LOT of unproven rookies and near-rookies actually hitting, which is a big ask. He smartly flipped Breece Hall and future scraps into a first and second, but the roster is thin on proven Cornerstones right now. When this thing blooms it could be terrifying, but right now it's more promise than production — a beautiful blueprint that still needs construction workers.

Josh Allen at the peak of his powers is the single most valuable fantasy asset in this entire league, and pairing him with Ashton Jeanty and James Cook gives Gavin a genuine win-now core that most owners would sell their soul for. The Foundational tier is also quietly deep with Garrett Wilson, Zay Flowers, Jaylen Waddle, and Bo Nix — this team has legitimate width. But trading away Tyler Shough and a first-rounder to get back Baker Mayfield and Garrett Wilson is the kind of lateral move that makes you wonder if Gavin is running the same offense for the next three years or just reshuffling the deck chairs on the Titanic. TE is a real weakness with Sam LaPorta leading the room, and that WR corps needs another star to emerge.

Joe Burrow, Jalen Hurts, and Amon-Ra St. Brown is a great core — on paper this is a team that should be a top-three squad. But the trade history is an absolute disaster: getting obliterated by Hernandez for over 4,800 in value and then losing another 2,172 to Sinykin in back-to-back weeks is the kind of trading record that gets you roasted at the league draft party. Zero first-round picks remaining after those heists, and Breece Hall is already old and declining in dynasty terms. The Mainstay-heavy roster means this team is more mediocre depth than true championship firepower below the top guys. GiantHawkTua is a contender the same way a Honda Civic is a sports car — it'll get you there, but don't bet on winning any races.

Bijan Robinson and Brock Bowers is one of the nastiest Cornerstone duos in the league, and Hernandez has been an absolute piranha in the trade market — winning every recent deal and extracting 2029 first-rounders out of GiantHawkTua like he was pickpocketing a tourist. Six first-round picks and a rebuild outlook means this team is aggressively hunting the future, but the WR room (Marvin Harrison and Jameson Williams as your top two) and QB situation (Jordan Love, C.J. Stroud, and GENO SMITH) are genuinely frightening in a bad way. The foundation is elite and the pick capital is ridiculous, but there is a LOT of roster construction left to do before this is a real championship threat. Hernandez is winning the trade war — now he just needs to win actual games.

Seth just executed one of the most audacious rebuild trades in recent league memory, flipping Jahmyr Gibbs to ekleiner for a haul of picks and depth pieces — turning a galaxy-brained deal that made the KTC calculator cry tears of value. Five first-rounders and a stockpile of Upside Shot players like TreVeyon Henderson, Jadarian Price, and Tyler Shough means Seth is betting big on the future, which is fine, but his best actual player is George Pickens, and his QB room is Tyler Shough, Aaron Rodgers, and Quinn Ewers, which sounds like a group project nobody wanted. This is a team that's going to be great in two or three years — maybe. Right now it's basically a farm team masquerading as a competitor, and George Kittle on short-term status sums up the vibe perfectly.

Selling Ja'Marr Chase — the highest-valued WR in the entire league — for picks and Ladd McConkey, and then immediately flipping McConkey for more picks, is either the most disciplined rebuild move of the offseason or the clearest sign of a white flag being raised. Seven first-rounders is truly outrageous pick capital, and Malik Nabers is a legitimate centerpiece to build around, but this roster is borderline unplayable right now — Fernando Mendoza and Dak Prescott at QB, Bhayshul Tuten leading the backfield, and Quentin Johnston as your WR2. There is one Cornerstone on this entire roster and it's a receiver whose team just replaced the guy throwing him the ball. Akracoon is betting it all on the draft gods, and if those picks hit, this column ages terribly — but right now this team couldn't outscore a bye week.

Justin Jefferson and CeeDee Lamb as a WR1-WR2 is absolutely filthy, and this is clearly a team trying to win NOW — but the rest of the roster screams 'desperate.' Christian McCaffrey is held together with tape and prayers, Saquon Barkley is on the wrong side of thirty, and Brock Purdy, Jared Goff, and Sam Darnold is the most anxiety-inducing QB room in the league. The TE position is a genuine embarrassment with Brenton Strange and Cade Otton as the options. With just one first-round pick and a trade history full of losses, GreyWaedekin is squeezing the last drops out of a window that is very visibly closing. This is a team that could absolutely flame out in 2026 and then spend the next three years wondering what happened.

Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes at QB is the most absurdly fun flex in this league, and yet somehow this team is ranked dead last — which tells you everything you need to know about how badly the roster falls off a cliff after those two. Zero future picks. ZERO. Not a single first, second, third, or fourth in the vault, meaning Herschey is playing chicken with the 2026 season with absolutely no safety net. Derrick Henry is one bad hamstring away from becoming a Short-term Memory, Travis Kelce and Dallas Goedert make the TE room look like a nursing home, and Daniel Jones is the QB3. Lamar and Mahomes are generational — but even they can't save you when your RBs are Derrick Henry and Josh Jacobs and you literally own no future draft capital. Bold strategy, Herschey. Hope the Lamar revenge tour is worth it.
